explanations.text:
# CREATE ABSTRACION
  you: "/human an http server using python that returns hello world"
       the first time you ask for code in a project with no human folder,
       claude starts you on human before anything else: you never type
       init, claude runs it                                    ([first use](First use))
       on a project with code, claude writes a short first global flow of
       the whole project, one numbered line per step, and leaves a tip on
       one line you would likely want to change; the reader opens on that
       line, lights it, and shows the tip under it
       on a project with no code, claude leaves a first abstraction as a
       draft in the human file welcome, not compiled, and the reader opens
       on it with the green compile button lit
       the tip goes away when you compile that file or click "got it"
       when you go on asking for code in the chat and not through human,
       claude refuses, gives you the reader, and tells you in two or three
       sentences how human works
       the tool registers the project first — the file list, the empty
       project map, the project id — so there is a place for your words before
       there is any code, and starts the reader                     ([the skill](human))
       ai harness hands your words to the project map as they are: no spelling
       fixed, no word trimmed; a pin goes in only when the thing it points
       at already exists, and a pin into nothing is refused; the entry is
       flagged as yours and keeps that first copy, with the pins taken out,
       as its origin
       ai harness writes the code files, no comments; the gate is static like a
       compiler's — the file must parse — and there is no run and no test
       when your words went onto code that was there before, ai harness syncs
       each changed file and the project map for your entry; the code was
       written for your words, so they follow the code and claude rewords
       nothing in them
       when your words hold no pin yet, claude hands them back with pins in
       them, through a plain retext; the gate strips the pins and compares
       the rest with the words it holds, character for character — one
       changed character is a refusal, so the pins go in and your words do
       not move; a pin that makes a circle over the maps is refused too
       your words and the code are the whole result: claude writes no
       telling of a file and no telling of the project unless you ask for
       one, and when you ask for one, ai harness takes the shape the catalog
       gives the file                                                    ([the shape](Explain))
       when you ask for the telling of one part and not the whole, claude
       puts it in a human file: a map with no code under it, over the files
       you choose, that answers to a bare name — payments — everywhere a
       file path goes, and may stand on another human file
       claude reports each file and the project, gives you the reader, and
       stays listening for what you write in it
       one human server runs on the machine: the register starts it, or hands the
       project to the one that runs, and the reader address carries the
       project id
                                                                      ([the run](The run))

# EDIT ABSTRACTION  you: "I would say it differently"
       your new words go in with --verbatim, pins and all; the origin is reset
       to them, and the entries that stood on the old words are marked stale

  you: change the code yourself, then "sync"
       claude rewords your abstraction only where the code forces it — the
       smallest edit, in your voice — and the tool warns you with the changed
       lines; the origin stays in the map, show marks the entry against it,
       and a retext --verbatim with the origin brings your words back

# WRITING ABSTRACTIONS ON WEB  you: write in the reader instead of the terminal
       every entry is a notepad: a click on its text opens it in place, in its
       raw form, pins and all, and a click outside, or Escape, draws it again;
       a file with no map offers you an abstraction or the code itself, and
       the empty project map offers a new abstraction      ([the writing](The reader writes))
       a right click on the file tree — on a file, on a folder, or on the
       empty space under them — opens a small list with "create file" and
       "create human", and a name box opens under the row you clicked
       "create file" takes a path from the root, folders and all, like
       src/app.py; a click on a folder, or on a file, puts the name you type
       inside that folder, and empty space takes the root, or the folder that
       space stands under; the file opens on a new abstraction, with no event,
       because nothing is left for claude to do
       "create human" takes a bare name — one word, no folder, no suffix —
       and makes a map with no code under it; the tool refuses a name
       another human file or a file at the root already holds, and this
       option queues no event either
       Escape, or a second pick of the same option, closes the box or the
       list, and a pick of the other option turns the box to that kind and
       empties it
       the file tree follows the files on disk, so a file claude writes
       shows without a reload
       once a map holds an entry that line is gone
       typing saves nothing; Ctrl+S keeps your draft in the browser, and the
       head bar says "unsaved" until you press it
       the "compile" button at the top right shows while a text differs from
       the map, and the map changes only when you press it
       the server runs the command you would have typed, one per changed text
       — a retext of your own words, a first telling, or the code written to
       disk — and a refusal comes back to you in the tool's own words; a pin
       in a first telling goes in when its target exists
       one event joins the queue; claude hears it through human watch,
       reads the diff of your words, writes the code they ask for, syncs
       every map that stood on them, with your words following the code and
       no word of them changed, pins the new sentences back in, and marks the
       event done with human ack
       a file made in the reader is empty and git holds no old copy of it,
       so its first sync runs against an empty old version
       when your words ask for a thing no file of the project holds, claude
       makes the file next to the others, outside the human folder, pins your
       words into it, and syncs the project map
       a delete needs no compile and no event: right-click an entry head, the
       head turns into a delete button with a cancel beside it, and one click
       takes the entry out at once, because nothing is left for claude to do
       the tool refuses the delete while another entry, the project map, or an
       open training row still stands on that entry

# DECOMPILE ABSTRACTION  
you: ask claude for a telling instead of writing one
       on a file with no map the open box carries a "decompile" button in
       place of your words, and one click asks claude for the whole-file
       telling
       on an empty file the server refuses the decompile, because your words
       come first and the code goes under them
       highlight words inside an entry and right-click "expand abstraction":
       a write space opens on top and its head is the button; words of your
       own go into the map first and claude writes the code under them, with
       none claude writes the expansion itself
       an expansion is a deeper telling of the words you highlighted; it
       stands above the entry, and the entry pins those words down into it,
       as a zoom on one block stands above the telling of the whole file
       right-click an entry head for "create abstraction": nothing to write,
       and claude tells the same thing again in plainer words below it
       a road you write nothing on queues the event alone
       when the machine is logged in to the training store, the server opens
       a training session if none is open for this project; claude writes
       two versions into a row and maps nothing, you pick one in a layer
       over the reader, and the close maps the pick
       a session belongs to you and to one project, the one whose id the
       tool wrote when it registered the project
       the pick of an expansion queues one more event, and claude pins the
       words you highlighted down into it
       with no login, or when the store does not answer, claude maps what
       it writes

[# EXPLAIN PINS](Pins)
  the pins tie a few words to a block, an earlier entry, another file, an
  entry of another file's map, or a map with no code under it; unique words,
  real targets, no circle anywhere among the maps, and an entry mapped
  before a pin points into it                                        

[# EXPLAIN SYNC](Rules)
  afterwards: sync runs exactly once per change, with --for when the change
  was written for the words of one entry, so that entry follows the code with
  no reword; then once more for the project map and once for every human
  file whose pins reach the change, and with --stale when a file's entry made
  your abstraction wrong, on the map the note names; an abstraction mapped
  before the flag existed takes the flag with a retext of its own text
